correctness.rationale: The structural proof reconstructs directly: any general-position set of size at least three excludes the center and uses at most one vertex from each arm, and every such choice is valid. Thus the coefficient in degree \(j\ge3\) is exactly the elementary symmetric polynomial \(e_j(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_k)\), while degrees zero through two count all subsets. For \(S(1,1,1,1,2,m)\), direct expansion gives the seven displayed coefficients and the two relevant inequalities place the unique nonunimodality threshold at \(m=15\). A fresh independent enumeration of every integer partition defining a spider through order 22 counted exactly 3374 types, with no nonunimodal type through order 21 and the sole order-22 failure \(S(1,1,1,1,2,15)\) with coefficients \((1,22,231,226,249,137,30)\). The finite enumeration is exhaustive for the stated cutoff and the all-spider formula is analytic.
